newsitem.title: USA: Intel rises on bullish sales outlook.
newsitem.headline: Intel rises on bullish sales outlook.

text.p: Intel Corp shares rose Tuesday after a Merrill Lynch & Co analyst said he expects the chipmaker's revenue growth to accelerate because of new products.
Shares of Intel, the world's biggest maker of computer chips, were up 2-7/8 at 157-5/8 in early afternoon Nasdaq trading of 3.95 million shares. The stock was the third-most active in U.S. markets.
Intel's revenue could rise 36 percent this year, compared with 30 percent historically, because of new chips and strong personal computer sales, said Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlak.
The company's earnings per share could rise 30 percent each year for the next five years, compared with growth of 25 percent in recent years, Kurlak said.

Intel introduced the Pentium II chip two weeks ago. The company has a slew of other high-speed microprocessors in the works. These chips will help Intel's average selling price per chip rise to $550 in the next five years from $276 currently, the analyst said.
Based on this growth prospect, the Santa Clara, Calif., company's share price could rise to $200 by the end of this year, and $235 by the end of 1998, he said.
